notes: THE FIX IS THE REMOVAL OF THE FIELD, not a better check. The save now carries ONE thing — `stood`, the body's own footprint as first-visit cell indices in walk order, zigzag-varint. The sightline raster and the place list are RE-DERIVED from it on load by the same two private methods observe() calls during play. `cells` and `places` are still written and still read, but read as a CLAIM to be checked: restore() reports every named place the footprint does not support (dropped) and every raster cell the blob claimed that the footprint does not paint (phantom_cells). Nothing in a blob can corroborate anything else in the same blob, which was the round-1 defect exactly.

Discovery.RESTORE_READS = ['stood'] is the whole channel from a blob into the model, published on the instance as `restoreReads`, and getUIState() derives `place_naming_parameters` from it rather than asserting it.

COST, RECORDED: observe() now paints from the CENTRE of the occupied cell rather than the body's exact position. That is what makes live play and replay bit-identical (R7) — the raster is a pure function of the set of occupied cells. Cell is 25 m, smallest built pad is 26 m, furthest any point sits from a cell centre is 17.7 m, so every place stays discoverable.
SIDE EFFECT, in our favour: the footprint is ~1 KB after a 557-cell walk against the 7 KB raster it replaces.

A NaN player position used to mark CELL ZERO as stood in (clamp(NaN) is NaN, NaN>>3 is 0, 1<<(NaN&7) is 1). Harmless while the raster was saved; corrupting once the footprint IS the save. Guarded in observe(). Found by R7 going red on a fixture that divided by zero.
LEGACY SAVES: a pre-round-2 blob has no footprint and comes back EMPTY, reporting legacy:true. Quietly trusting the old raster for old saves would leave the hole open.

LIMIT, stated: forging the FOOTPRINT itself is not refused (R8 records it). That is a different claim — 'I walked the whole province', whose map is the honest map of that walk — not 'put a square on a place I have not been', which is what S35 forbids and is now impossible. There is no field left in which a place can be NAMED.

RI-UIX02 K1 was red at HEAD for two rounds and the r1 verdict called it 'a five-minute decision that is currently sitting as a red gate'. Both exemptions I added are declared judgement calls a critic should feel free to overturn; the reason I was willing to make them is F6, which encodes §B's actual concern ('a coordinate ON A QUEST RECORD') as a property rather than as a directory list, and which fires inside the placement roots.

referred.what: The P.6 remedy gives `swap_left`/`swap_right` a SECOND MEANING while a screen is open and no fight is live: walk the advertised destination list. The ACTION SET IS NOT WIDENED — both are two of RI-JRN03 §A's closed fourteen, already bound on keyboard (3/4, wheel), pad (D-pad L/R) and touch, so no fifteenth verb and no new binding. What changes is the meaning, contextually, which is the same shape the file already uses for `roll` ('back' out of a fight, a dodge in one). In combat they are untouched, because `swap_left` is half of the offhand chord (input-map.json off.r1.*) and RI-UIX03 P6 requires the fight to stay playable with the screen up. Declared at runtime as getUIState().nav.walk_actions / walk_live so it is a number a probe reads rather than a claim in a comment. Raising it rather than landing it silently, per the brief.

The r1 verdict's acceptance — 'getUIState().map.mutator_arities lists EVERY state-writing method with EVERY arity 0' — cannot be met by the save path: restore() has to receive the blob. mutator_arities is now enumerated from the prototype and fail-closed (an accessor or a named reader is a reader; anything else is a state writer), and it reports `restore: 1` honestly. The property that actually matters is reported alongside and is stronger: `place_naming_parameters`, derived from Discovery.RESTORE_READS, is empty. Asking for that substitution to be ruled on.

findings_for_other_pieces: game/src/render/interior.js — `bla_prison_block` does `Object.assign(B.grate(P), { position: new THREE.Vector3(0,0,0.2) })`. `position` is a read-only accessor on THREE.Object3D, so this throws `Cannot assign to read only property position` out of Province._buildTile and kills any teleport whose build ring reaches Blackrose. Uncommitted in the working tree (game/src/render/exterior.js is untracked alongside it), so this is the settlements/exterior builder mid-edit. Fix is `.position.set(0,0,0.2)`. NOT TOUCHED — their claimed file.

game/src/combat/enemy.js:303 — EnemyController._idleBehaviour throws `this.ai.step is not a function` on ANY fixed step with a streamed enemy alive. It took two runs of my probe down before I stepped one frame at a time and cleared hostiles around it. Uncommitted; the enemy-AI rebuild (W1-12) is in flight. NOT TOUCHED.

tools/analysis/ui-layer.mjs ui_combat_neutral — aggro('deadwater-koor-nakh'): no such entity. listEntities() is returning an entry whose eid aggro() rejects. The tool wraps the call in try/catch and it does not help, because tools/lib/browser.mjs exits the process on a harness throw; that is worth someone fixing, because it means NO tool can survive a harness error it has already anticipated.

tools/harness/w1-13-r4-input-only.mjs still reports ["inventory","journal","world"] and `levelup by input = false` after this fix, and that is a TRUE report of what it measures: its pass 2 visits only screens ONE press from the world and never recurses, while the ring is seven screens long and levelup is five steps from the inventory. I did not edit their file. N1b in my probe is the same recipe taken to a fixed point and reaches all six; the difference between the two numbers is itself the finding, and a critic should check my closure rather than take it.
